content_sections.body_text: Live has /ɪ/; leave has /iː/. Relax your tongue for /ɪ/. Move it higher and forward for /iː/; this sound is often longer too. Say live–leave five times. Change mouth shape and length, not length alone.
content_sections.title: 1. Two vowels (8 min)

content_sections.body_text: B: ‘I live here.’ A: ‘Did you say leave?’ B: ‘No, live—/lɪv/.’ A: ‘Oh, you live here.’ Read both roles, then cover them and speak again. B clearly repeats the word that A heard wrongly.
content_sections.title: 2. Clear repair (8 min)

content_sections.body_text: For listening, use text-to-speech only to play a hidden order of live and leave; write L or E, then reveal it. TTS speaks; it does not hear you. For speaking, say one word to an independent listener or a speech-recognition tool that displays the recognized word. If neither is available, write ‘not checked.’ Your own replay is practice, not proof.
content_sections.title: 3. Two kinds of check (10 min)

content_sections.body_text: Make a four-line talk: give one fact, hear one word wrongly, ask ‘Did you say …?’, then correct it. Speak both roles. Success: the reply answers the question and an independent listener or suitable speech-recognition tool identifies live or leave. If unavailable, mark ‘not checked’ and keep the recording as practice.
content_sections.title: 4. Take turns (9 min)
